title: Machine-Checked Exact-Integer Dichotomy, Matroid-Intersection, and Parameterized WSAT Certificates for Connectivity Switching in Graphs
abstract: Christoph Kern, Alexander Firbas, and Manuel Sorge (arXiv:2611.32927, November 24, 2026) established a comprehensive algorithmic and complexity classification for Local-Con Switching and Global-Con Switching in switch graphs, including a complete-multipartite P-vs.-NP dichotomy for {1*}-bounded switches (Theorem 1), polynomial-time weighted Global-Con Switching via graphic-and-partition matroid intersection with shifted edge weights (Theorems 7-8), W[SAT]/W[1]-hardness via series-parallel WSAT switch graphs and a tight 5|E(H)| Partitioned Subgraph Isomorphism reduction (Theorems 3-5), and a 4*lambda {1,1}->{2,1} K_{1,*} gadget (Theorem 6). We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and exact-Z certificate auditor for the combinatorial, primal-dual, and reduction core of these results. An 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 5 zero-axiom theorems) formalizes complete-multipartite K2+K1-freeness, alternating transition-path lengths, Edmonds matroid-intersection weak duality and rank obstructions, Theorem 8 shifted-weight telescoping, Lemma 4 structural Boolean formula semantics, PSI 5|E(H)| tightness, and Theorem 6's backward 4*min_i c'_i <= sum c'_i total budget bound. SWITCH-GRAPH-CONN-CERT-1.0 audits four exact modes—including both YES spanning trees and NO Edmonds rank obstructions—replaying 16 canonical certificates in 0.030-0.160 ms, passing exhaustive 41-graph dichotomy and 224-assignment Lemma 4 checks, and rejecting 57/57 live adversarial forgeries.
